reading.title: Exam pressure
reading.text: Students in many Asian countries face intense pressure to do well in university entrance exams. Some study for twelve hours a day, and doctors report rising rates of depression among teenagers. Psychologists warn that students who suppress their stress, rather than express it, are most at risk. Some schools now run weekly sessions where pupils talk openly about their feelings. The early results are impressive: students in these schools report lower stress and, surprisingly, slightly higher marks.
